official.deadline_note: The only date published anywhere in the Authority notice is 30 August 2026, and it binds the ECOWAS nominating agency (email the scanned National Endorsement Form to info@scholarships.gov.gh, then courier the paper file to the Director-General via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, P.O. Box M53, Accra). The notice's own 'Deadline' field reads 'Not specified' and no applicant-side closing date is given.
official.status_note: The Authority published the call on 03 June 2026 as an 'Official notice' with status 'Official notice' and deadline 'Not specified'. The single published date (30 August 2026) has passed and the participating institutions' academic year began September 2026, so the published 2026 round is no longer open to new applicants; no 2027 round notice had been posted as at the verification date.
benefits: Award of scholarships by the Government of the Republic of Ghana for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate studies in Public Tertiary Education Institutions in Ghana for the 2026/2027 academic year
Maximum duration of award of 4 years (Undergraduate), 2 years (Masters) or 4 years (Ph.D.)
Nomination by the applicant's ECOWAS member state through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ghana)
eligibility: Be citizens of ECOWAS member states other than Ghana
Meet the admission requirements of the attached list of participating universities
Demonstrate academic excellence and leadership potential
Demonstrate commitment to contributing to national or regional development
Meet immigration and visa requirements for international students studying in Ghana
requirements: Have applied for at least one full-time on-campus programme at a public tertiary institution in Ghana

Attach either (a) a conditional offer (letter of admission) from the chosen university OR (b) an acknowledgement notice from a Ghanaian public tertiary institution that the application for a seat has been made and the appropriate application fee has been paid
Submit academic credentials, admission letters and supporting documents via the Ghana Scholarships Authority online portal at www.scholarships.gov.gh
Be nominated by the designated Nominating Agency in the applicant's ECOWAS member state; individual applicants cannot self-nominate
documents: Conditional offer / letter of admission from a Ghanaian public tertiary institution, or the institution's acknowledgement notice that a seat application was made and the application fee paid
Supporting documents submitted through the Ghana Scholarships Authority online portal
National Endorsement Form completed and signed by the nominating agency, recording each candidate's name, programme of study, programme level (Undergraduate, Masters or Ph.D.) and passport number
coverage: The notice describes the award only as a Government of Ghana scholarship for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate study at public tertiary education institutions in Ghana for the 2026/2027 academic year; it does not state whether tuition, living costs, accommodation or travel are covered
application_method: STEP 1: apply for at least one full-time on-campus programme at a Ghanaian public tertiary institution and keep proof of a conditional offer/admission letter or of the paid application acknowledgement
STEP 2: submit academic credentials, admission letters and supporting documents via the Ghana Scholarships Authority online portal (www.scholarships.gov.gh / apply.scholarships.gov.gh)
STEP 3: the Authority carries out initial review and shortlisting for onward submission to the designated Nominating Agency in the applicant's ECOWAS member state
STEP 4: nomination by the ECOWAS member state based on its quota, national priority and other considerations

STEP 5: nominees are returned to the Ghana Scholarships Authority by the member state through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ghana) using the National Endorsement Form, by email to info@scholarships.gov.gh and by courier to the Director-General, Ghana Scholarships Authority, Accra
official.application_route: No direct individual application is possible: secure a Ghanaian public-tertiary admission or paid-application acknowledgement, upload evidence through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal, and be nominated by your ECOWAS country's nominating agency (3 nominees per state, 42 in total).
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of an ECOWAS member state other than Ghana; nomination is routed through the applicant's home-country nominating agency, and applicants must meet immigration and visa requirements for international students studying in Ghana
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Awards are made in fields aligned with regional development priorities: Science, Technology and Innovation (engineering, computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, cybersecurity, renewable energy); Health and Medical Science (medicine, nursing, public health, biomedical sciences); Agriculture and Food Systems (agribusiness, crop science, animal science, food technology); Trade, Economics and Business (economics, finance, entrepreneurship, international trade, AfCFTA-related studies); Governance and Public Policy (public administration, law, international relations, peace and security studies); Environment and Climate Studies (climate change, environmental management, natural resource governance, marine and blue economy studies)
official.duration: Undergraduate: 4 years; Masters: 2 years; Ph.D.: 4 years (maximum duration stated in the notice)
official.description: The Government of the Republic of Ghana is offering scholarships for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate studies at public tertiary education institutions in Ghana to qualified students from ECOWAS member states for the 2026/2027 academic year. Awards are made in fields aligned with regional development priorities, and each ECOWAS member state nominates up to three candidates through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ghana).
official.region: Ghana (West Africa), open to ECOWAS member states

verification.notes: Checked the full text of the Ghana Scholarships Authority PWASI 2026 notice (published 03 June 2026), the Authority's opportunities index, the programmes pages (including ECOWAS Scholarship Pathways), the FAQ, the local scholarship guidance and the application portal sign-in page; the notice publishes no monetary figure, no coverage breakdown and no English-language requirement, and its deadline field reads 'Not specified'. The only date in the notice, 30 August 2026, is the nominating agencies' National Endorsement Form deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a Government of Ghana award for citizens of ECOWAS countries other than Ghana to study full-time and on-campus at a listed Ghanaian public tertiary institution, and the notice deliberately publishes no cash value, no stipend figure and no statement about tuition or living costs. Because the Authority never states what the money buys, treat any amount you see quoted on an aggregator or blog as unverified and ask the Authority directly at info@scholarships.gov.gh before you spend money on the application. The single gate that matters is nomination: only three candidates per ECOWAS member state (42 in total) are put forward, and they are chosen by your own government's nominating agency, not by Ghana. That means your real competition is inside your country's ministry, and the workable strategy is to get on that agency's shortlist before the 30 August deadline the notice sets for endorsement forms.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An ECOWAS national (non-Ghanaian) who already holds or is finalising an admission to a listed Ghanaian public university in one of the six priority field clusters, and whose home ministry/scholarship agency can be persuaded to nominate them within a three-person national quota.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify and write to your country's designated nominating agency early - the notice names no agency, so expect it to be the Ministry of Education, Foreign Affairs or a national scholarships board, and confirm the office by phone or email

Apply to at least one listed Ghanaian public tertiary institution and pay the application fee, keeping the acknowledgement notice as your proof; the listed windows have already closed for some institutions, so confirm next-cycle dates on each institution's own admissions page
Register on the GSA portal (apply.scholarships.gov.gh) and upload credentials, admission evidence and supporting documents before nominating agencies finalise their lists

Match your intended programme to one of the six published priority field clusters - economics, finance, entrepreneurship, international trade, law, international relations and public administration are all listed, so social-science applicants are not excluded
Have your passport details ready, because the National Endorsement Form requires each candidate's passport number and only three names fit per country
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to the Authority and waiting: the notice states individuals cannot self-nominate, so a portal submission without agency nomination will not reach the awarding stage
Being nominated with an incomplete file - the notice says explicitly that nomination of ineligible applicants or with incomplete supporting documents will not be considered
Applying to a private university, an online programme or an off-campus programme, all of which fall outside 'full-time, on-campus' study at a 'public tertiary education institution'
Submitting a paid-application acknowledgement without the required proof, or losing the receipt before the agency completes the endorsement form
Missing the quota: if your country's agency fills its three slots with candidates whose programmes are closer to its own national priorities, a strong application can still be left out
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not itemised in the official notice. Assume you will fund the Ghanaian institution's application fee (paid before any scholarship decision), student visa and immigration costs, flights to Ghana, accommodation and living expenses, and any non-tuition academic user fees, unless and until an award letter states otherwise.
document_audit: The admission proof is an either/or: a conditional offer letter OR an acknowledgement notice of a paid seat application - do not attach a mere registration screenshot with no evidence of payment
Names and passport numbers must be identical across the admission letter, portal submission and the National Endorsement Form; inconsistencies are the fastest way to lose a slot
The National Endorsement Form is completed by the agency, not by you, so build in time to send it back and forth rather than assuming it can be fixed at the deadline
Paper applications are couriered to the Director-General through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra, so keep a complete duplicate set - a lost courier costs you the nomination
alerts: The notice's own 'Deadline' field says 'Not specified'; the only date, 30 August 2026, is the nominating agencies' deadline to return National Endorsement Forms, not an applicant deadline - plan backwards from it

Institution windows differ widely (UDS closed 31 May 2026, UCC 31 July 2026, University of Ghana 14 August 2026), so an applicant who waits for the scholarship call can miss the admission that is a precondition for the award
Ghanaian citizens are excluded by design, and the award cannot be combined with another route for the same study
The Authority warns that no individual, group or third party is engaged to assist applicants and that the service is free - treat any agent demanding payment for PWASI placement as fraudulent
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You apply to a listed Ghanaian public university first and pay its application fee, upload that admission evidence plus credentials on the GSA portal, the Authority shortlists and forwards files to your ECOWAS nominating agency, and the agency returns up to three endorsed nominees by email and courier to Accra by 30 August.
